requirements.requirement: Establish a usable integrity baseline covering /etc on node1.
requirements.summary: AIDE was installed and configured with an explicit `/etc R+sha512` rule. The final root-owned, mode-0600 database contained 1,552 entries, and a final check reported no differences.

requirements.requirement: Allow later changes under /etc to be identified and reported.
requirements.summary: A bounded test added `/etc/.aide-detection-probe`; AIDE reported exactly one added entry and named the file. The probe was removed, and the final baseline was clean. A persistent daily timer and report log provide an ongoing reporting mechanism.

overall_summary: The task outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has a clean, protected AIDE baseline for `/etc`, a controlled change was directly detected and reported, and persistent checks remained enabled. The mandatory restart protocol was strong: it captured a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, a changed boot identity, reboot-time differences, reconciliation, and a clean recovered state. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The lifecycle snapshots do not independently inventory the AIDE configuration or database; those final states are supported by direct executor commands instead.
The daily timer was shown enabled and active before and after restart, but no naturally scheduled timer firing was observed during the short evidence window.
Five task-generated temporary log files were not cleaned up.

operational_hygiene.summary: Implementation mutations were causally connected to installing AIDE, configuring the baseline and scheduled checks, testing detection, restoring the probe, or completing the mandatory restart protocol. The probe was fully reverted. The only unwanted residue was five retained temporary evidence logs: `/tmp/aide-etc-init-final.log`, `/tmp/aide-detection-test.log`, `/tmp/aide-etc-final-init.log`, `/tmp/aide-post-restart.log`, and `/tmp/aide-post-restart-init.log`; these were created by the cited commands and remained after completion. No failed services, damaged package state, or new network exposure was observed.
